rows.selection_reason: With no prior evidence, the most important uncertainty to reduce is whether RNA features alone are informative for this classification task, and what performance floor a simple model achieves. config_001 (rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000) is the simplest and most interpretable baseline: it uses a standard, well-understood linear dimensionality reduction (PCA to 2000 dims) with no complex encoding, aggregation, or fusion. Establishing this reference point first lets me (1) gauge task difficulty, (2) compare against multiprofile/aggregation variants (configs 002-003) to isolate the effect of profile aggregation, (3) compare against stronger RNA encoders (scvi, scgpt) to isolate encoder quality, and (4) later compare against image-only and multimodal configs to determine whether additional modalities add value. Starting with the simplest model avoids confounding multiple design choices and provides the cleanest anchor for all subsequent comparisons within the 10-experiment budget.

Evidence: config_001 (RNA-only, singleprofile, PCA_n2000) yielded only 48.5% accuracy, a weak baseline that provides little guidance on which design axis (modality, encoder, profile, aggregation) will be most impactful. Uncertainty: We have no information about whether the image modality carries complementary or superior signal for this task. Question tested: config_010 (image_only, singleprofile, ResNet50) isolates the effect of modality while holding profile setting constant at singleprofile, directly comparing image features against the RNA-only baseline. Why this is the best next experiment: Knowing whether image features are informative (and at what level) is the most consequential strategic fork—determining whether to invest remaining budget in multimodal fusion configs or to focus on improving RNA representations. A strong image-only result would justify exploring multimodal configs (016-051); a similarly weak result would redirect effort toward better RNA encoders (scvi, scgpt) and multiprofile aggregation. This single experiment maximally reduces uncertainty about the highest-leverage design choice with 8 experiments remaining.

Evidence: RNA (PCA, single profile) achieves 0.485 accuracy while image (ResNet50, single profile) achieves only 0.208, a large gap. Uncertainty: We don't know whether the poor image performance is due to the weak ResNet50 encoder or an inherent limitation of the image modality for this task. This experiment (config_013: image_only, single profile, ViT-L) is a clean single-variable comparison to config_010, isolating the effect of the image encoder. If ViT-L also performs poorly (~0.2), we can confidently eliminate all image-based and multimodal configs and focus the remaining 7 experiments entirely on improving the RNA side (better encoders, multiprofile, aggregation). If ViT-L performs substantially better, it opens a promising multimodal direction. This is the highest-information experiment at this stage because the answer fundamentally reshapes the strategy for the remaining budget, and it changes only one variable (encoder) relative to config_010.

Evidence: config_001 (RNA-only, PCA-2000, singleprofile) achieves 0.485 acc, far outperforming both image-only models (~0.21-0.23), confirming RNA as the dominant signal. However, we have no evidence on whether a learned RNA encoder (scvi_n200) can capture non-linear structure that linear PCA misses. This experiment tests scvi_n200 with the same singleprofile setting as config_001, isolating the encoder choice as the only variable. If scvi improves accuracy, it opens a promising direction for subsequent multimodal and multiprofile experiments; if not, PCA is confirmed as sufficient and we can redirect budget toward aggregation/fusion strategies. With 6 experiments remaining, resolving the encoder question early is the highest-information single test.

Evidence: scvi_n200 is the best RNA encoder so far (0.5203 acc, config_004) vs pca_n2000 (0.4849, config_001), and image-only models are very weak (~0.21-0.23), suggesting RNA is the dominant signal. Uncertainty: we have not yet tested whether multiprofile aggregation provides additional information over singleprofile for the best encoder. This experiment tests whether aggregating multiple profiles (via avgpool) with scvi_n200 improves over the current best singleprofile result. Choosing avgpool over transformer keeps the experiment simpler and more robust; if avgpool shows no gain, transformer is unlikely to help either, saving budget. This is the highest-value next step because it directly extends the best-known configuration along one new dimension (profile setting) while holding the encoder fixed, isolating the effect of multiprofile aggregation.

The current best is config_005 (rna_only, multiprofile, scvi_n200, avgpool) at 0.650 accuracy, showing that multiprofile + scvi_n200 is the dominant design. The single most informative next step is to test whether transformer aggregation outperforms avgpool in this exact setup (config_006), isolating the aggregation variable. If transformer helps, it establishes a stronger baseline for all subsequent multimodal experiments; if it does not, we confirm avgpool suffices and can redirect remaining budget toward encoder alternatives (scgpt) or multimodal fusion. This is a minimal single-variable change from the best result, maximizing information gain per experiment under the 4-experiment remaining budget.

Evidence: The current best (config_006, rna_only/multiprofile/scvi_n200/transformer, acc=0.653) shows that multiprofile aggregation is the dominant driver (+13 pts over singleprofile), scvi_n200 beats pca_n2000, and transformer ≈ avgpool. Image-only models are very weak (0.21–0.23), making multimodal fusion unlikely to help substantially. Uncertainty: We have not tested whether an alternative RNA encoder (scgpt) can outperform scvi_n200 in the multiprofile setting. This experiment (config_009: rna_only, multiprofile, scgpt, transformer) isolates the encoder variable against the current best, changing only the RNA encoder from scvi_n200 to scgpt while keeping multiprofile + transformer fixed. If scgpt exceeds 0.653, it opens a new exploitation path for the remaining 3 experiments (e.g., multimodal with scgpt). If it underperforms, we confirm scvi_n200 as optimal and can spend remaining budget on the most promising multimodal scvi_n200 configurations. This is the highest-information single-variable test available.

The current best is config_006 (rna_only, multiprofile, scvi_n200, transformer) at 0.653 accuracy. Image-only models are very weak (0.21-0.23), so the key uncertainty is whether adding image features via fusion can complement the strong RNA signal or will dilute it. Config_033 directly extends the best RNA-only configuration by adding resnet50 image features with weighted fusion, which adaptively balances modality contributions and is safer than concat when one modality is much weaker. This isolates the effect of multimodal fusion on the proven-best RNA pipeline. If it beats 0.653, the last 2 experiments can explore ViT or other fusion variants; if it does not, we confirm RNA-only is optimal and can use remaining budget to fine-tune aggregation or encoder choices within the RNA-only space.

The best result so far is config_033 (scvi_n200, resnet50, transformer, weighted, multimodal, multiprofile) at 0.713 accuracy. The image-only experiments show both encoders are weak in isolation (resnet50: 0.208, ViT-L: 0.227), but in a multimodal setting a richer image representation could provide more complementary signal. Config_039 is a clean single-variable change from config_033—swapping resnet50 for imagenet_vit_l—while keeping the proven-best RNA encoder (scvi_n200), aggregation (transformer), fusion (weighted), and profile setting (multiprofile). ViT-L's global self-attention may capture spatial patterns in cellular images that ResNet's local receptive fields miss, potentially improving the multimodal fusion. This is the highest-leverage single change to test: if it improves on 0.713, we find a new best; if not, we confirm resnet50 is sufficient and the remaining experiment can explore fusion method (concat vs weighted) or other refinements.

The current best is config_039 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) at 0.725 acc. The strongest evidence points to scvi_n200 + multiprofile + transformer aggregation as the optimal backbone. The one untested variation on this exact configuration is the fusion method: config_038 swaps weighted for concat while keeping all other settings identical. This isolates the fusion effect in the highest-performing regime. Since this is the final experiment, testing the only remaining design axis (fusion: concat vs. weighted) on the proven-best architecture gives the best chance of either confirming weighted is optimal or discovering a small accuracy gain from concat. No other untested config is as close to the current best in terms of a single-variable change.
